inventory_label: Normal Account UI can only advance a lock. Closed years cannot be reopened.
audit_status: AUDIT COMPLETE — source and isolated PostgreSQL scope
reference_status: Inventory policy verified; no new visual reference supplied. Browser/native interaction and production mutation not tested.

findings.classification: Lock-through date does not cover the full calendar day
findings.current_behavior: A date-only lock is stored at UTC midnight. validateContext compares entryDate <= lockedThrough, while postingSchema accepts timestamps. A same-day noon journal posted successfully after setting a date-only lock.
findings.required_correction: Use one defined business-date convention across all posting and lock checks. Reject or normalize timestamp input and enforce an inclusive whole-day cutoff consistently.
findings.evidence: Actual PostgreSQL service reproduction: lockedThrough 2031-10-31; entryDate 2031-10-31T12:00:00.000Z returned POSTED. Local synthetic data only.

findings.classification: Irreversible lock advancement lacks a review and actionable Web feedback
findings.current_behavior: Web submits directly through advancePeriodLockAction without confirmation, pending guard or accountAction error handling. Reason input lacks server minlength 3. Native uses free-text dates and an unfiltered active-year picker including CLOSED years; it does not show the existing cutoff or irreversible impact in the lock dialog.
findings.required_correction: Add explicit year/current cutoff/new cutoff review and irreversible-impact confirmation, pending protection and field-level domain errors; limit native choices to open eligible years and use validated date controls. Preserve server-side restrictions.
findings.evidence: Source inspection of period-lock page, account-finalization action, FinancialYearScreen and shared periodLockSchema. No browser/native tap or reference screenshot comparison performed.

findings.classification: Same-date retries produce duplicate lock audit events
findings.current_behavior: The service permits an equal lock date and always upserts and appends PERIOD_LOCKED. Two identical requests generated two audit rows. The Web date min includes the existing cutoff.
findings.required_correction: Treat an identical already-applied lock as a no-op or define retry identity; distinguish a genuinely new advance and retain reliable actor/date change history.
findings.evidence: Actual isolated PostgreSQL reproduction: two identical calls, two PERIOD_LOCKED rows.

findings.classification: Native lock editor ignores write capabilities
findings.current_behavior: FinancialYearScreen always shows New, including period-lock mode, although the overview exposes canManagePeriods. ACCOUNTANT has ACCOUNT_LEDGER_VIEW and can load overview but lacks ACCOUNT_PERIOD_LOCK; server correctly denies the write.
findings.required_correction: Gate the native lock editor with canonical server capabilities and preserve the existing endpoint permission check.
findings.evidence: Native source plus accountingOverviewForActor capabilities and shared permission map. This is a dead-action UX issue, not an authorization bypass.

verified_existing_controls: Company lock serializes posting, period changes and year close.
Closed financial years remain closed and reject posting.
Web and mobile mutation entry points require ACCOUNT_PERIOD_LOCK; native dead actions do not bypass it.

verification.scope: Three audit reproductions plus three existing close-books tests on disposable loopback *_ci PostgreSQL. Positive reproduction tests assert current defective behaviour; passing does not mean defects are fixed.
